fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is killed as stated. Gray decoding is nonlinear and no emitted integral lift makes decoded-port equality a lattice gluing condition; bent correlation and Construction-A coset leaders also do not certify the augmented NAND/COPY lattice against unrestricted signed combinations.

Proposal 2 is killed as stated. Cut descriptions of Voronoi-relevant vectors do not by themselves define NAND/COPY selectors, centers, gluing, or the complete composed transfer operator, and the proposed K6 search leaves those objects unspecified.

Proposal 3 is the sole continuation, but only after repair. Variables Q and h describe squared distances only if the extended Gram containing the target is positive semidefinite, and the proposed enumeration of arbitrary subsets of {-1,0,1}^8 is not an executable bounded search.

Proposal 4 is killed. Primitive configurations modulo GL_d(Z) are not finite without determinant or coordinate bounds, and evidence through rank four could not establish the claimed unrestricted Cartesian-port no-go.

Proposal 5 is killed by a mechanism error. Positive minimum cycle mean gives additive excess linear in path length; it does not yield the multiplicative squared-energy recurrence or exponential ratio required by the recursive shell theorem.

Proposal 6 is killed as stated. Total unimodularity gives conformal circuit decomposition for kernel vectors, not for DROP, wrong-port, or nonzero-residual states, and nonorthogonal quadratic energy is not lower-bounded merely by decomposing a vector into circuits.
evidence: The supplied verifiers leave arbitrary nonseparable Gram synthesis open: Generation 5 rejected only coordinate-separable D4 metrics, while Generations 33–34 rejected only one exterior-tag family. Generation 7 closes affine ports on one E6 shell but expressly leaves augmented encodings open.
No supplied verifier tests any of the six new proposals. Consequently none has experimental support, and prior finite passes or failures cannot be promoted to a general Voronoi or hardness statement.

For a fixed finite codebook and emitted linear port map, Proposal 3's distance constraints are linear in an extended Gram. Exact diagonal-dominance bounds can provide positive definiteness and a uniform finite tail bound, after which unrestricted minima and depth-two transfer tables are genuinely decidable.

Only repaired Proposal 3 directly tests the ROADMAP frontier requirements of equal completeness, global outside-codebook coercivity, unrestricted transfer closure, and the exact 65/64 ratio in one bounded experiment.
next_experiment: Freeze repaired Proposal 3 at D=8: use canonical one-hot legal selectors for the four NAND words and two COPY words, four zero-port auxiliary columns, and explicit integral port maps with emitted equality gluing. Search exact rational extended Grams H=[[Q,-h],[-h^T,s]] with entries bounded by 64, strict diagonal-dominance margin at least 1, and legal squared energy 64; the uniform coercive bound must determine the complete finite Fincke–Pohst core before optimization. Build exact transfer tables for every Boolean port and certify every nonbinary port by the tail bound; reject unless both tiles have matching legal radii, unrestricted closure, and exact depth-two lambda/mu at least 65/64. A pass authorizes only a subsequent symbolic tile proof, not recursion or hardness.
